title: Diffusionless mechanisms produce diffusion-like electrochemistry in battery particles - Nature Energy
gist: A Nature Energy research briefing argues that low-frequency overpotentials in Li-ion active particles, long attributed to solid-state lithium diffusion, can instead arise from electrolyte penetration into agglomerate particles that makes interior surfaces electrochemically active in a transmission-line configuration — producing diffusion-like electrochemistry with no diffusion involved. It is a short summary of Kapate et al., so the supporting data are not in the accessible text.

insights.claim: Low-frequency overpotentials in lithium-ion battery active particles, long attributed to solid-state diffusion, can be produced entirely without diffusion by electrolyte penetration into agglomerate particles acting as a transmission line.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: If the canonical diffusion signature is an artefact of particle architecture, rate-capability roadmaps built on 'faster-diffusing' cathode chemistries may be optimizing the wrong variable.
insights.quote: This mechanism for accessing battery capacity produces diffusion-like electrochemistry, even without diffusion involved.

insights.claim: Electrolyte that penetrates into battery agglomerate particles makes the particles' interior surfaces electrochemically active, giving an additional route to accessing battery capacity beyond bulk solid-state transport.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Reframes secondary-particle morphology and electrolyte wetting as levers on usable capacity and rate — a formulation and particle-engineering advantage rather than a materials-chemistry one.
insights.quote: electrolyte penetration in battery agglomerate particles is shown to make interior surfaces electrochemically active, but with a transmission-line configuration

insights.claim: The apparent Warburg coefficient of agglomerate battery particles depends on electrolyte composition and charge-transfer resistance — dependencies a true solid-diffusion process should not exhibit.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete falsification test labs and cell makers can run on their own impedance data before trusting published diffusivity numbers.
insights.quote: Dependence of the apparent Warburg coefficient of agglomerate particles on electrolyte composition and charge-transfer resistance.

insights.claim: Reported lithium diffusivity values in battery active materials show large unexplained discrepancies, per a critical review of the galvanostatic intermittent titration technique cited in the briefing.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Diffusivity figures in startup and supplier datasheets carry method risk; ask which technique produced them and whether particle architecture was accounted for.
insights.quote: This review analyses the discrepancies in reported Li diffusivity values in battery active materials.
insights.locator: References, Kang, S. D. & Chueh, W. C. (2021)

insights.claim: Lithium heterogeneity in layered oxide cathodes is dominated at the inter-particle rather than intra-particle scale, implying particle kinetics are surface-reaction controlled rather than bulk-diffusion controlled.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Supports a shift in cathode design priority toward surface/interface chemistry and electrode-scale uniformity over shrinking primary particle size.
insights.quote: Li heterogeneity is dominated at the inter- rather than intra-particle scale, suggesting that the particle kinetics are surface-reaction controlled
insights.locator: References, Park, J. et al., Nat. Mater. 20, 991–999 (2021)

insights.claim: Complex internal heterogeneity in battery particles undermines the simplified single-particle representations that underpin standard battery models, according to a News & Views cited in the briefing.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Battery digital-twin and BMS state-estimation vendors relying on classical single-particle diffusion models face a modelling-accuracy risk as this picture propagates.
insights.quote: This News & Views article explains the implications of complex heterogeneity on simplified representations of battery particles.
insights.locator: References, Kang, S. D. & Chueh, W. C., Nat. Nanotechnol. 18, 1130 (2023)
